text: Euclid's proof of the infinitude of primes forms N = p₁p₂···p_k + 1 from a finite list of primes. What is the correct conclusion about N?
choices: N has a prime factor not in the list, since N leaves remainder 1 when divided by each p_i
N is divisible by every p_i in the list
N is composite and equals the next prime after p_k
explanation: N ≡ 1 (mod p_i) for each listed prime, so no p_i divides N; yet N > 1 must have some prime factor, which is therefore a new prime. Crucially N itself need not be prime (the common misreading in option A), and it is certainly not divisible by the listed primes.
